groups.title: Robots
groups.blurb: The three hostiles. Each is modelled, rigged with joint empties and animated in Blender; the game plays the same clips and adds aim, hit reactions and wrecks on top.

items.name: Spider
items.text: A four-legged walker with a twin-gun turret. It walks the dungeon cell to cell, turns by stepping, and its feet are re-solved every frame so they stay planted when it is shot. Turn is played backwards for a right turn.

items.name: Drone
items.text: A twin-rotor drone with a gun slung under its body. Shot down, it spins out of control for a few seconds, falls and explodes where it lands.

items.name: Ceiling turret
items.text: Hangs from a rail in the ceiling. In the game it is a gatling: it winds up for 0.85 s, then fires 16 to 20 rounds from the firing part of its Shoot clip.

groups.title: Weapons and hands
groups.blurb: The two first-person views: gun, gloved hands and sleeves, posed and animated together. The arms are rigged (MakeHuman CC0 base mesh and skeleton); the gloves are modelled on them. Open them in the player's view to see them as the game frames them.

items.name: Pistol
items.text: Service pistol with a reflex sight and a weapon light; 15 rounds, unlimited magazines. Slide, trigger and magazine are animated parts; the hands are re-solved on every frame of every clip.

items.name: Machine gun
items.text: Machine gun with a holographic sight and a status screen; 30-round magazine. Fire is five rounds of climb then five that loop while the trigger is held; two reloads (tactical, and from empty with the bolt catch).

groups.title: Environment set: structure
groups.blurb: The modular kit every dungeon is assembled from: 4 m cells, 2 x 3 m wall panels, 1 x 2 m floor tiles, 2 x 2 m ceiling panels. Wear and dirt are baked into the vertex colours and drawn by the paint shader.

groups.title: Environment set: equipment and cover
groups.blurb: What stands in the rooms. Each room theme (lab, storage, server, power, workshop) picks its own; nothing against a wall is deeper than 1.3 m, so robots and the player can always pass.

items.name: Crate
items.text: Cover-height crate.

items.name: Barrier
items.text: Low barrier for cover.

items.name: Specimen tank
items.text: Its liquid takes the room theme's colour in the game.

items.name: Training cage
items.text: Holds the training dummy in the first room: bars 0.84 m apart that stop the player but not bullets.

groups.title: Exit, loot and pickups
groups.blurb: What a run is for: crates to open, what they give, and the portal in the deepest room.

items.name: Exit portal
items.text: Stands free in the middle of the deepest room; stepping in completes the mission.

items.name: Loot crate (health)
items.text: E opens it; the lid's cyan lamp goes dark.

items.name: Med kit
items.text: Carried (up to three), used with H for +40.

items.name: Health pack
items.text: +35 health on pickup.

items.name: Ammunition box
items.text: +60 machine-gun rounds.

groups.title: Concept scene
groups.blurb: Where V2 started: one detailed lab room built and rendered in Blender as the target look, before anything was taken into Godot. It is now the title screen's backdrop.

items.name: Concept lab room
items.text: Walls, floor tiles, mezzanine and stairs, specimen tanks, cable trays and ceiling lights, exported from v2/scene.blend.
